name: Chauka (Odissi square stance)
summary: The square: feet wide and fully turned out, knees open, weight even — the masculine stance of Odissi.
setup: Face the phone about 2.5 m away, camera at hip height. Feet a little wider than the hips and turned out, knees bent straight out over the toes, arms out to the sides at shoulder height with the elbows bent. The body makes a square. Hold.
brief: Feet a little wider than the hips and turned out, knees bent straight out over the toes, arms out to the sides at shoulder height with the elbows bent. The body makes a square.
why: From the front the two knee angles and the width between the knees are both direct reads, which is exactly what a chauka is judged on.
calibrationPose: Standing tall, feet apart, before you sit into the square.
enterCue: Sit into the square — knees wide over your toes
tempo: Sit over 2 s, hold, rise over 2 s.
progression: Longer holds; add the arm positions and head movements.
contraindications: Knee or groin pain; hips that cannot turn out without the back arching.

faults.label: Not sitting deep enough
faults.tip: The chauka is a deep, even sit. A shallow version loses the square shape entirely.

faults.label: Knees closing in
faults.tip: The knees travel out over the toes to hold the square. Closing them puts the load on the inside of the knee.

faults.label: Weight sliding to one side
faults.tip: The square is symmetrical. A hip that drifts sideways means one leg is resting.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Arching to force more turnout moves the strain to the lower back. Reduce the turnout instead.

faults.label: Arms dropping
faults.tip: The arms hold their line at shoulder height for the whole hold — that is part of the stance.

guide.stop: Knee or groin pain; a lower back that will not stop arching.
guide.cannotSee: How far the feet are turned out, and whether the weight is truly even.

points.t: Feet wider than the hips, turned out from the hip joints.
Knees bent out over the toes, thighs opening to the sides.
Spine vertical, tailbone tucked, weight even on both feet.
Out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows bent, palms forward.
